#FLUX: --queue=compute
#FLUX: --nodes=6
#FLUX: --tasks-per-node=12
#FLUX: --time-limit=8h

bash /home/sfan19/.bashrc

echo $FLUX_JOB_ID
echo $USER

# Get the hostname of the rank 0 task to serve as the scheduler address
SCHEDULER_HOST=$(flux exec -r 0 hostname)
echo SCHEDULER: $SCHEDULER_HOST

# Start the dask scheduler on the rank 0 task in the background
flux exec -r 0 dask-scheduler --port=8786 &
sleep 5

# Use flux run to start dask workers on all allocated nodes in the background
# One dask-worker command is run per node, which then starts 12 processes (--nprocs 12).
flux run -N ${FLUX_JOB_NNODES} --tasks-per-node=1 dask-worker --nprocs 12 --nthreads 1 $SCHEDULER_HOST:8786 &
sleep 5 # Give workers time to start and connect

#!/bin/bash -l
#SBATCH --nodes=2  --time=04:00:00  
#SBATCH -C gpu 
#SBATCH --account m1759
#SBATCH --gres=gpu:8
#SBATCH --exclusive
#SBATCH -c 80

module load pytorch/v1.4.0-gpu
module list
export HDF5_USE_FILE_LOCKING=FALSE

nodes=$(scontrol show hostnames $SLURM_JOB_NODELIST) # Getting the node names
nodes_array=( $nodes )
worker_num=$(($SLURM_JOB_NUM_NODES - 1))

master_node=${nodes_array[0]}

for ((  i=0; i<=$worker_num; i++ ))
do
  node_i=${nodes_array[$i]}
  srun --nodes=1 --ntasks=1 -w $node_i python -m torch.distributed.launch --nproc_per_node=8 --nnodes=8 --node_rank=$i --master_addr=$master_node train.py --run_num=13 &
  pids[${i}]=$!
  echo "Training started on node $i"
done

# Wait for completion
for pid in ${pids[*]}; do
    wait $pid
done

date

module load pytorch/v1.4.0-gpu
module list
export HDF5_USE_FILE_LOCKING=FALSE

# The master address is determined by the hostname of the rank-0 task in the allocation

# The original script's manual loop over srun is replaced by a single flux run command.

flux run -n 2 -N 2 --tasks-per-node=1 python -m torch.distributed.launch \
    --nproc_per_node=8 \
    --nnodes=2 \
    --node_rank=$FLUX_NODE_RANKID \
    --master_addr=$MASTER_ADDR \
    train.py --run_num=13

date

#BSUB -J NET-seq

set -o nounset -o pipefail -o errexit -x

# Function to run snakemake
run_snakemake() {
    local snake_file=$1
    local config_file=$2

    args='
        -oo {log.out} 
        -eo {log.err} 
        -J {params.job_name}
        -R "rusage[mem={params.memory}] span[hosts=1]"
        -n {threads} '

    snakemake -n \
        --snakefile $snake_file \
        --drmaa "$args" \
        --jobs 100 \
        --configfiles $config_file
}


# Run pipeline to process mNET-seq reads
pipe_dir=src/pipelines
samples=SAMPLES.yaml

snake=$pipe_dir/NETseq.snake
config=NETseq.yaml

run_snakemake $snake "$samples $config"

config=pauses.yaml

    local config_file=$2

    # NOTE: The DRMAA arguments have been converted from LSF to Flux syntax.

    args=' \

        --error={log.err} \
        --job-name={params.job_name} \
        --nodes=1 \
        --cores={threads} '

    snakemake -n \
        --snakefile $snake_file \
        --drmaa "$args" \
        --jobs 100 \
        --configfiles $config_file
}

NPROCS=16

source ~/init.sh
make clean && make
rm -r hpctoolkit*

hpcstruct --gpucfg yes hpctoolkit*
hpcstruct --gpucfg yes jacobi
hpcprof -S jacobi.hpcstruct -I jacobi.cpp -I jacobi_kernels.cu -I ./+ hpctoolkit*
echo "===DONE==="
